entities.summary: Alric was a king of the Saxon kingdom of Kent, jointly with Æðelberht II and Eadberht I, from approximately 796 to 800 CE. He played a crucial role in maintaining the unity of the kingdom during a period of significant political turmoil in Anglo-Saxon England. Alric's reign was marked by the establishment of a robust system of governance, which included the creation of a powerful nobility and the promotion of trade and commerce. His leadership helped to secure the kingdom's borders and foster economic growth, laying the groundwork for the kingdom's future prosperity. The legacy of Alric can be seen in the many institutions and traditions that were established during his reign, including the Kentish mint and the Anglo-Saxon church. As a key figure in the history of Kent, Alric's impact extends far beyond his own lifetime, shaping the course of Anglo-Saxon history and leaving a lasting legacy in the region. This can be seen in the numerous archaeological finds and historical records that attest to his reign, including the famous ' Kentish Cross' which is now housed in the British Museum. The influence of Alric's reign can also be seen in the development of the English language, with many place names and surnames derived from the Old English language that was prevalent during his time. As a result, Alric's significance extends far beyond his own lifetime, making him one of the most important figures in the history of Kent.
